THE DIAGRAMS AT THE TOP OF AN OPEN ARTICLE

Ten of them. Four try to draw a human body out of thin bezier curves on graph paper, and those are the four that look wrong — the side-sleep figure reads as a blob with a circle stuck to it.

Board 2 offers two ways out. Board 3 is the whole set drawn the way I would do it. Board 4 puts one back in the real modal, which is the comparison that counts.

MIXED ON PURPOSE

Silhouette for the two where the subject is a person doing something — sleeping, tummy time. Schematic for the other eight, including the latch, where drawing a body buys nothing and costs comfort.

Three of these have no drawing at all today and fall through to the generic squiggle: sickness, the dating scan, and movements.
